intro: Don't copy a trend. Pick one format, add your own idea to it, and make it feel like yours. Formats that break out usually pair a real human idea with an AI effect.

platformTips.tip: Completion rate matters most. Keep it tight, usually 15 to 35 seconds, and cut anything that doesn't earn its place.
Trending audio and saves help a lot. Make something people want to keep, like a tip, a template or a pretty loop.
The very first frame decides whether people stay. Start on your strongest image, not a title card.

hooks.name: Contradiction
hooks.text: Everyone says [COMMON ADVICE]. Here's why it doesn't work for [AUDIENCE].

hooks.name: Start mid-story
hooks.text: She had 3 minutes before [EVENT]. Then [SURPRISE] happened.

hooks.name: Stop doing this
hooks.text: Stop doing [COMMON MISTAKE] if you want [RESULT].

hooks.name: Result first
hooks.text: This took me [SHORT TIME] with free tools. Here's exactly how.

hooks.name: Relatable pain
hooks.text: If you've ever [PAINFUL SITUATION], this is for you.

hooks.name: Challenge
hooks.text: I tried [THING] every day for [N] days. Here's what changed.

formats.name: Claymation mini-scenes
formats.why: The handmade clay look feels warm and nostalgic, so people share it without the uncanny feeling that realistic AI sometimes gives.
steps: Pick one tiny story, such as a clay fruit seller whose mango rolls away.
Generate 3 or 4 still images using the same style words every time.
Animate each image for 4 to 5 seconds.
Add small sound effects and gentle music.
Add a caption and post.
formats.prompt: Stop-motion clay animation of [SUBJECT] [ACTION] in [SETTING]. Visible thumbprints, soft studio light, slight handmade imperfections, shallow depth of field. Vertical 9:16. No text.
hooks: This tiny clay seller has a big problem...
Watch what happens when the clay mango rolls away.
formats.watchOut: Keep your character identical across shots. Paste the same character description into every prompt.

formats.name: Cute 3D character portraits
formats.why: People love seeing themselves, their pets or their products as cartoon characters, so they comment, share and ask how you did it.
steps: Choose a subject you have the right to use: yourself, your pet or your product.
Ask for a stylised 3D cartoon version in an original design.
Make 3 versions with different outfits or moods.
Show a quick before and after, real photo then character.
End with a question that invites people to ask for their own.
formats.prompt: Turn [SUBJECT, e.g. my pet cat] into a cute stylised 3D cartoon character: big expressive eyes, soft studio lighting, pastel background. Original character design, not a copy of any film character. Keep the real [FEATURE, e.g. orange fur] recognisable.
hooks: I turned my cat into a cartoon. Look at the eyes.
Comment your pet and I'll make it next.
formats.watchOut: Don't ask for a named studio's look or any copyrighted character. Get permission before using photos of other people, and never use photos of children without a parent's consent.

formats.name: Painterly everyday scenes
formats.why: Ordinary moments, such as a market morning or rain on a zinc roof, look magical as hand-painted animation. These get saved and shared.
steps: List 5 everyday moments your audience recognises.
Generate one painted still for each.
Animate gentle motion only: wind, rain, steam, moving clouds.
Add soft music or the natural sound of the scene.
Caption it with a feeling, not a description.
formats.prompt: Hand-painted 2D animation of [EVERYDAY SCENE], watercolour backgrounds, soft pastel palette, gentle wind moving hair and leaves, calm mood. Original art style. No text.
hooks: Your Monday morning, but painted.
A Lagos market at 6am, as a painting.
formats.watchOut: Don't name a living artist or a studio in the prompt. Describe the look instead.

formats.name: Talking objects
formats.why: A face and a complaint make an ordinary thing instantly funny, and it doubles as a gentle way to tell a product story.
steps: Pick an object people have strong feelings about, like a kettle, a generator or a phone charger.
Write a 3-line complaint in its voice.
Generate the object with an animated face, talking to camera.
Add a voiceover and captions.
End with a punchline or a tip.
formats.prompt: A [OBJECT, e.g. kettle] with a natural animated face, [EMOTION] expression, talking to camera about [COMPLAINT]. Soft kitchen light, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16.
hooks: My kettle has filed a complaint.
If your generator could talk, it would say this.
formats.watchOut: If it's an ad, say so. Don't make health, money or results claims through a cartoon voice.

formats.name: What-if scenarios
formats.why: AI is perfect for answering strange questions that used to need a film budget. One odd idea, treated as completely normal, is easy to understand and easy to share.
steps: Write 10 what-if ideas and pick the funniest or most visual.
Treat it as normal: no big reaction from the people in the scene.
Generate 2 or 3 short shots.
Add a calm, serious voiceover.
Ask viewers for their own what-if.
formats.prompt: Realistic scene of [ABSURD IDEA] treated as completely normal, documentary camera style, [LOCATION], natural light. No text.
hooks: What if buses had a VIP wing?
What if your village had a rush hour?
formats.watchOut: Make it obvious it's imaginary. Never make realistic fake clips about real events, real people or breaking news.

formats.name: Cinematic mood clips
formats.why: Slow, beautiful camera moves work as stand-alone mood pieces and as B-roll inside longer videos.
steps: Pick a place and a time of day.
Choose one camera move only, such as a slow push-in.
Generate 3 variations and keep the best.
Colour-grade lightly and add ambient sound.
Use it as an opener or as B-roll in a longer video.
formats.prompt: Slow [CAMERA MOVE, e.g. push-in] through [PLACE] at [TIME OF DAY], [WEATHER], shallow depth of field, natural film grain, realistic. No people's faces. Vertical 9:16.
hooks: Sunrise over the old market.
A quiet street, 5am.
formats.watchOut: Realistic AI scenes need the platform's AI label. Don't present them as footage of a real event.

formats.name: Cozy loops
formats.why: A calm, endlessly repeating scene is made to be watched again and again, and people leave it on as background.
steps: Choose a cosy scene: rain at a window, a cat by a lamp, a quiet kitchen.
Generate a short clip with only slow motion.
Loop it so the end flows back to the start.
Add calm sound you have the right to use.
Give each loop its own theme and title.
formats.prompt: Cozy [SCENE], slow ambient motion, [WEATHER], warm interior light, loopable, no story, soft colour grade. Vertical 9:16.
hooks: Rain on the window. Stay a while.
Your 30-second reset.
formats.watchOut: Posting dozens of near-identical loops looks mass-produced. Vary the theme and add something personal.

formats.name: 90-second explainer
formats.why: Dense, well-edited explainers get strong saves and shares because people feel smarter after watching.
steps: Pick one question people actually ask.
Write the script: hook, four facts, one surprising detail each.
Record or generate the voiceover.
Add a map, chart or simple graphic every 10 seconds.
Put your sources in the caption.
formats.prompt: Write a 90-second explainer script about [TOPIC]. Hook in the first 3 seconds, 4 facts with one surprising detail each, a map or chart moment every 10 seconds, and a question at the end. Flag every claim I should verify.
hooks: Why does [CITY] look like this?
The real reason [THING] costs so much.
formats.watchOut: Fact-check every claim yourself. Name your sources in the caption.

formats.name: Original-song music video
formats.why: A catchy original hook with matching visuals is shareable, and it's yours, so you own the sound people reuse.
steps: Write a short chorus about one clear idea.
Make the song with a tool whose licence allows commercial use.
Write a six-scene visual treatment.
Generate each scene using the same character description.
Cut to the beat and post the song as its own sound.
formats.prompt: Write a 30-second visual treatment for a song called [TITLE] in [GENRE] with 6 scenes. For each: what happens, the camera move, and a one-line AI video prompt using this character: [CHARACTER].
hooks: I wrote a song about [IDEA] and made the video myself.
Sing along: it only has one line.
formats.watchOut: Check the music tool's commercial licence. Don't imitate real artists' voices or use their lyrics.

formats.name: Local skit animation
formats.why: Everyday situations told in your own language and humour travel fast with local audiences, and few creators do them well with AI.
steps: Pick one relatable situation: the bus, the landlord, market bargaining, the family group chat.
Write setup, escalation and punchline.
Give two characters distinct looks and voices.
Animate one scene per line of dialogue.
Add captions in the language you speak.
formats.prompt: Write a 30-second animated skit in Nigerian Pidgin about [SITUATION]. Two characters: [CHARACTER 1] and [CHARACTER 2]. Setup, escalation, punchline. Keep it playful with no insults about tribes, religion or disability. Then give a one-line video prompt per scene.
hooks: Every family WhatsApp group has this person.
Market bargaining, but make it a movie.
formats.watchOut: Have a native speaker check the language. Avoid stereotypes and don't imitate real people.

formats.name: Absurd character shorts
formats.why: Silly, over-serious characters are made to be quoted and remixed. It's a crowded fad, so the creators who last give their character a personality and a story.
steps: Invent one character with a name, a flaw and a catchphrase.
Generate it in the same setting each time.
Write a 3-line scene where it takes something very seriously.
Add a voiceover.
Post a series, not a one-off.
formats.prompt: [IMPROBABLE CREATURE] wearing [FUNNY ACCESSORY], named [MADE-UP NAME], standing in [SETTING], realistic render, extremely serious expression, vertical 9:16.
hooks: Meet [NAME]. He has strong opinions.
[NAME] explains why Mondays are illegal.
formats.watchOut: A crowded fad. One-off posts rarely build an audience, and templated uploads can be demonetized. Give your character a real story.

formats.name: UGC-style product demo
formats.why: Product videos that feel like a real person talking to their phone, built for small businesses and affiliates.
formats.teaser: Includes the script structure, the visual prompt, the disclosure wording, and a testing plan for 5 versions of one product.

formats.name: Series engine
formats.why: A repeatable system for one character, one world and 30 episodes without losing consistency.
formats.teaser: Includes a character bible template, an episode planner, and a batch-production checklist.

formats.name: Retention edit recipe
formats.why: A cut-by-cut editing pattern that keeps people watching to the end.
formats.teaser: Includes pacing maps, caption styles, and a before/after example of a flat edit and a tight edit.

formats.name: 30-day format calendar
formats.why: A month of posts that rotates these formats so you never stare at a blank page.
formats.teaser: Includes daily prompts, hook choices for each day, and a weekly review sheet.

formats.name: Trend adaptation checklist
formats.why: A quick test for whether a trend fits you, and how to make it original instead of a copy.
formats.teaser: Includes a 10-question fit test, a rights and safety check, and ways to make any trend your own.
